about: The Power-to-Weight Calculator determines the power-to-weight ratio of a vehicle, a critical metric for acceleration performance and overall vehicle dynamics. This ratio is fundamental in automotive performance analysis.
Understanding power-to-weight ratios helps compare vehicles across different classes and predict acceleration performance regardless of absolute power or weight figures.
howToUse: Enter vehicle power in HP or kW
Input vehicle weight in lbs or kg
Compare with other vehicles or performance targets

faqs.question: What's a good power-to-weight ratio?
faqs.answer: Sports cars typically have 8-15 lb/hp, supercars 5-8 lb/hp, and hypercars under 5 lb/hp. Lower numbers indicate better acceleration potential.

faqs.question: How does power-to-weight affect acceleration?
faqs.answer: Lower power-to-weight ratios generally mean faster acceleration. A 10% improvement in ratio can reduce 0-60 times by roughly 8-10%.

faqs.question: Should I focus on adding power or reducing weight?
faqs.answer: Weight reduction affects handling, braking, and acceleration equally. Adding power only improves acceleration and top speed. Weight reduction is often more cost-effective.

faqs.question: How do I calculate curb weight vs race weight?
faqs.answer: Curb weight includes all fluids and standard equipment. Race weight may exclude passenger seats, spare tire, and include safety equipment. Use the weight that matches your application.
